Barry, looking up from his phone, says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: Nine hundred quid. For a box room. Then he puts the phone face down on the table. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: his voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Use the image as the scene. A British comedy film with English actors. Barry, nodding at something on a television above the camera, says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: Another boat last night. Where are they all going to live? 'Cause it ain't round here. I can't afford round here. Then he takes a swig of tea. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: his voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Use the image as the scene. A British comedy film with English actors. Barry, with a sour look, says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: You sound like my daughter. Then he goes back to his breakfast. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: his voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Use the image as the scene. A British comedy film with English actors. Denise, wiping the counter, says, in a dry, flat northern English accent: Mine's gone up again. The café and the flat. Then she keeps wiping in small circles. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: her voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Use the image as the scene. A British comedy film with English actors. Denise, without stopping wiping, says, in a dry, flat northern English accent: It's not the boats, Barry. It's the landlord. Put mine up twice this year. And the council's put my rates up for the privilege. Then she looks up. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: her voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Use the image as the scene. A British comedy film with English actors. Denise, deadpan, says, in a dry, flat northern English accent: Your daughter's right. She still lives with you. Then she holds still with a flat look. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: her voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Use the image as the scene. A British comedy film with English actors. Denise, not looking up, flatly, says, in a dry, flat northern English accent: Bloody landlord. Then she keeps wiping. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: her voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Use the image as the scene. A British comedy film with English actors. Barry, holding up the little Freddo, says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: Least something's still cheap. Then he looks at it fondly. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: his voice, café clatter, a radio murmuring. No music. Thanks.

Use the image as the scene. A British comedy film with English actors. Barry, holding up the little Freddo, outraged, says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: Twenty p? Bloody boats. Then he keeps staring at the card. Fixed camera, one continuous shot. Sound: his voice, café clatter. No music. Thanks.

Rain runs slowly down the outside of the window glass. Across the road the bank's gold windows stay lit and the street stays empty. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: rain on glass, a kettle coming to the boil, cutlery, a radio murmuring with no words. No dialogue. No music. Thanks.

Rain falls steadily through the orange lamp light and ripples the puddles. Inside the gap of the door, a shadow passes once across the warm light. The door stays as it is. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: heavy rain, a distant crowd roaring in the next street, a pallet truck rattling somewhere inside. No dialogue. No music. Thanks.

The man at the shelves pushes the brick of notes the last few inches into the shelf and pats it once. The man with the clipboard makes one tick on his clipboard. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: paper sliding on steel, a pen tick, the hum of a bulb, a crowd roaring faintly far above. No dialogue. No music. Thanks.

The hands push the brick of notes the last inch home, flush with the others, then let go and draw back out of frame. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: polymer notes sliding on steel, a soft thud, the hum of a bulb. No dialogue. No music. Thanks.

Rain beads slide slowly down the outside of the glass and the street-lamp reflections shimmer. The cards behind the glass stay still. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: rain on a shop awning, a car passing on wet tarmac. No dialogue. No music. Thanks.
